issues.label: Climate Tipping Point
issues.summary: Planetary systems approaching irreversible thresholds — ice sheet collapse, permafrost methane release, AMOC shutdown

_authored.detail: Global thermoregulation overwhelmed — feedback loops accelerating beyond compensatory capacity
Ice sheet mass loss exceeding regeneration rates, albedo feedback accelerating warming
Precipitation patterns shifting — drought and flood extremes intensifying simultaneously
Carbon sinks saturating — forests transitioning from net sink to net source in some regions
Ecosystem models projecting cascading failures across interconnected tipping elements
Atmospheric composition shifting beyond Holocene baseline — novel climate states emerging

issues.label: Mass Extinction Event
issues.summary: Species loss rates 100-1000x background levels — sixth mass extinction accelerating across taxa

_authored.detail: Biodiversity collapsing at all trophic levels — insect biomass, amphibian populations, coral reefs declining
Threat detection systems overwhelmed by simultaneous extinction drivers across all habitats
Soil microbiome diversity declining, reducing nutrient cycling and plant community resilience
Wetland habitats degraded — critical breeding and migration stopover sites lost
Conservation policy failing to keep pace with extinction acceleration — resource allocation inadequate
Environmental monitoring detecting novel extinction cascades faster than management can respond

issues.label: Ocean Acidification
issues.summary: Marine pH declining from CO2 absorption — shell-forming organisms and coral reef systems collapsing

_authored.detail: Ocean carbonate chemistry shifting — aragonite saturation dropping below shell-formation thresholds
Ocean heat absorption altering thermohaline circulation patterns and global heat distribution
Marine biodiversity crashing — coral bleaching, plankton decline, fishery collapse cascading through food webs
Pollution-ocean interaction amplifying — industrial runoff compounding acidification stress on marine life
Polar ocean chemistry changing fastest — cold water absorbs more CO2, Arctic ecosystems most vulnerable

issues.label: Deforestation Crisis
issues.summary: Global forest loss exceeding regrowth — Amazon, Congo, and Southeast Asian rainforests approaching dieback thresholds

_authored.detail: Forest carbon sink collapsing — mature forest loss releases stored carbon and eliminates future sequestration
Habitat fragmentation isolating populations — genetic bottlenecks and local extinctions accelerating
Soil exposed to erosion and degradation after canopy removal — nutrient cycling disrupted
Regional precipitation patterns disrupted — deforested areas receiving less rainfall, drying further
Wetland systems downstream degraded by sedimentation and altered hydrology from upland clearing
Land-use policy captured by agricultural and extractive interests — conservation undervalued

issues.label: Toxic Contamination

_authored.detail: Pollution detection systems revealing contamination far more widespread than previously known

Aquatic chemistry altered by industrial discharge — endocrine disruptors detected across water systems
Wetland filtration capacity overwhelmed by volume and persistence of novel contaminants
Sensitive species eliminated by toxin exposure — pollinator and amphibian populations in sharp decline
